newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses sharply lower, hit by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses sharply lower, hit by Wall St.

text.p: European bourses opened sharply lower on Wednesday, depressed by a wave of profit-taking on Wall street which sent U.S. stocks tumbling to their biggest loss in five months.

On currency markets, the dollar weakened in early trading after its giddy rally to a 23-month peak against the mark on Tuesday. Sterling also fell on fears that its recent strength could harm British industry.
The losses on European bourses ended a record-breaking pace on much of the continent this week as investors saw the recent strength of the dollar as a boon to exporters.

London, Frankfurt and Paris shares got off to a poor start with investors nervously digesting the close on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones industrial average lost 79.01 points, or 1.21 percent, to close at 6,442.69.
Huge computer-driven sell programmes in New York kicked in during a frantic last 10 minutes of trading to lock in profits after the Dow rose 500 points, or eight percent, in November.
"We haven't been following Wall Street up...we have been following it down...but I don't think it will be a disaster by any means," said a dealer in London.
The gloom in London, where stocks fell 0.34 percent, was slightly offset by the the weaker pound which was seen as helping the exporting sector.
"Sterling is an important factor. If it weakens, it will help a lot of major stocks. So there are other things at work here besides Wall Street," the dealer said.

But European markets will remain edgy ahead of the U.S. employment data for November, due on Friday, which can provide pointers on how the world's biggest economy is faring and thus the direction of U.S. interest rates.
French stocks took the biggest knock from Wall Street, sliding 1.6 percent in early transactions after a strong performance this week.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down to 2311.99 points at one stage. Alcatel Alsthom fell 2.72 percent to 462.2 francs following news that the government has suspended the Thomson SA privatisation.
Frankfurt, which hit its fourth record close on Tuesday on the stronger dollar, fell 0.6 percent, sapped by Wall Street's fall and the weaker dollar.
"It's going to be consolidation today, based on where the dollar is going," one trader in Frankfurt said.
The dollar slipped under 1.56 marks, weighing on exporting chemical and auto stocks. BMW, Hoechst and BASF were all lower after surging on Tuesday.
The U.S. currency slid by a pfennig in early European trading as the dollar took a breather after its record-breaking pace. It recovered a little by mid-morning.
"People are sitting back. They are waiting to see what happens now," said a trader at British bank.
The mark was more buoyant amid figures showing Germany's economy expanded by one percent in the third-quarter after a 1.5 percent increase in the previous quarter.

"They are pretty robust figures on the whole. After a very strong second-quarter the economy seems to be doing very well. It is definitely accelerating back to trend," said Klaus Baader, senior currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Sterling was another focus on currency markets as it struggled to recover after a bout of profit-taking overnight pushed it to one-month lows at 1.6410 against the dollar.
"We needed a good bout of profit-taking...Everyone went for the exit together," said the trader. The pound was at $1.6403 in initial trade after $1.6452 on Tuesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.23 yen and 1.5603 marks against 113.68 yen and 1.5647 marks in late Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 9.4 points at 4,052.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 36.37 points at 2,312.74.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 17.94 points at 2,869.40.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $370.40 an ounce, compared to the close on Tuesday of $$367.85. Silver was firmer at $4.80, up nine cents.
